mcqs.question: Which procedure does a 2025 International Journal of Colorectal Disease publication describe as effective for rectal prolapse and associated pelvic floor disorders?
mcqs.explanation: The 2025 paper states robotic ventral mesh rectopexy (RVMR) is an effective technique for rectal prolapse and associated pelvic floor disorders.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Robotic ventral mesh rectopexy (RVMR) is an effective technique for addressing rectal prolapse (RP) and associated pelvic floor disorders.

mcqs.question: A woman with pelvic organ prolapse reports straining and incomplete evacuation. Which NICE recommendation applies?

options.B: Investigate only if she also has urinary symptoms
options.E: Don't investigate; bowel symptoms are expected

mcqs.explanation: NICE: in women with POP, consider investigating symptoms of obstructed defaecation or faecal incontinence (with baseline FI assessment per the FI guideline).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider investigating the following symptoms in women with pelvic organ prolapse: urinary symptoms that are bothersome and for which surgical intervention is an option; symptoms of obstructed defaecation or faecal incontinence (see the recommendations for baseline assessment of faecal incontinence in the NICE guideline on faecal incontinence in adults ); pain; symptoms that are not explained by examination findings. [2019]

mcqs.question: Which surgical repair does NICE recommend offering for posterior vaginal wall prolapse?

options.A: Sacrocolpopexy with mesh as first choice

mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer posterior vaginal repair without mesh to women with a posterior vaginal wall prolapse.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer posterior vaginal repair without mesh to women with a posterior vaginal wall prolapse. [2019]

mcqs.question: What does NICE interventional procedures guidance say about transvaginal mesh repair of posterior vaginal wall prolapse?

options.A: Use as the first-line standard repair
options.B: Use only in the context of research
options.C: Use whenever native-tissue repair is declined
options.D: Use routinely with concurrent continence surgery

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Use only in the context of research
mcqs.explanation: Serious but well-recognised safety concerns and inadequate long-term efficacy evidence mean it should only be used in the context of research.

sourceRefs.excerpt: '1.1 Current evidence on the safety of transvaginal mesh repair of anterior or posterior vaginal wall prolapse shows there are serious but well-recognised safety concerns. Evidence of long-term efficacy is inadequate in quality and quantity. Therefore, this procedure should only be used in the context of research.

mcqs.question: A woman has faecal incontinence and coexisting pelvic organ prolapse. What conservative treatment does NICE suggest considering?

options.C: Supervised PFMT for at least 4 months
options.E: Two weeks of unsupervised pelvic floor leaflets

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Supervised PFMT for at least 4 months
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least 4 months for women with FI and coexisting POP.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider a programme of supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least 4 months for women with faecal incontinence and coexisting pelvic organ prolapse.

mcqs.question: When assessing suspected complications after mesh surgery, which examination does NICE suggest performing, if indicated?

options.B: Proctoscopy at every follow-up visit for at least 5 years
options.C: Rectal exam for mesh perforation or fistula

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Rectal exam for mesh perforation or fistula
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider a rectal examination, if indicated, to assess for mesh perforation or fistula.

sourceRefs.excerpt: consider performing a rectal examination, if indicated, to assess for the presence of mesh perforation or fistula

mcqs.question: Which lifestyle advice does NICE suggest for women with pelvic organ prolapse?

options.A: Weight loss if BMI >30, less lifting, treat constipation
options.D: Bed rest and avoiding all exercise until symptoms have fully settled

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Weight loss if BMI >30, less lifting, treat constipation
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider advice on losing weight if BMI over 30, minimising heavy lifting, and preventing or treating constipation.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider giving advice on lifestyle to women with pelvic organ prolapse, including information on: losing weight, if the woman has a BMI greater than 30 kg/m 2; minimising heavy lifting; preventing or treating constipation. [2019]

topics.topicKey: brain metastases stereotactic radiosurgery vs whole-brain radiation vs resection
topics.topicDisplayName: Brain metastases: stereotactic radiosurgery vs whole-brain radiation vs resection
topics.coverageNote: Pool: NICE NG99 brain tumours/metastases (no stored year), NICE NG14 melanoma imaging (2022), ASCO-SNO-ASTRO 2022, ASTRO 2022, and trials (RTOG 9508, Chang 2009, EORTC 22952 relapse data, Brown/N0574 cognitive data, BREAK-MB background). Some trial rows contain only the design, so the questions use the stated results only.

mcqs.question: A patient has a single brain metastasis and good performance status. What does NICE suggest?

options.A: Observation with repeat MRI in 3 months before deciding on any treatment
options.D: Maximal local therapy: surgery, SRS or SRT
options.E: Systemic therapy alone in all cases

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Maximal local therapy: surgery, SRS or SRT
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider maximal local therapy with surgery, stereotactic radiosurgery or stereotactic radiotherapy for a single brain metastasis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider maximal local therapy with either surgery, stereotactic radiosurgery or stereotactic radiotherapy for people with a single brain metastasis.

mcqs.question: After stereotactic radiosurgery to a single brain metastasis, what's the NICE position on further radiotherapy?

options.A: Repeat SRS to the same lesion at 3 months
options.B: Adjuvant WBRT within 4 weeks for all patients
options.C: Adjuvant WBRT if the primary is lung

mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer adjuvant WBRT to people with a single brain metastasis treated with SRS/SRT or surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer adjuvant whole-brain radiotherapy to people with a single brain metastasis treated with stereotactic radiosurgery or radiotherapy or surgery.

mcqs.question: Which patients with multiple brain metastases does NICE suggest considering for stereotactic radiosurgery or radiotherapy?

options.A: Only those who have had WBRT already
options.B: Only those with more than 20 lesions
options.E: KPS below 50, whatever the disease status

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider SRS/SRT for multiple brain metastases with controlled or controllable extracranial disease and KPS of 70 or more, taking into account the number and total volume of metastases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider stereotactic radiosurgery or radiotherapy for people with multiple brain metastases who have controlled or controllable extracranial disease and Karnofsky performance status of 70 or more. Take into account the number and total volume of metastases.

mcqs.question: A patient with NSCLC has brain metastases unsuitable for surgery or SRS and a Karnofsky performance status of 60. What does NICE recommend about WBRT?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer WBRT to people with NSCLC and brain metastases unsuitable for surgery or SRS/SRT with a KPS under 70.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer whole-brain radiotherapy to people with: non-small-cell lung cancer and brain metastases that are not suitable for surgery or stereotactic radiosurgery or radiotherapy and a Karnofsky performance status of under 70.

mcqs.question: A patient with multiple brain metastases is starting WBRT. Under what circumstances does NICE allow concurrent systemic therapy to enhance its efficacy?

options.D: Whenever there are more than 4 lesions

mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer concurrent systemic therapy to enhance WBRT efficacy in multiple brain metastases unless as part of a clinical trial.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer concurrent systemic therapy to enhance the efficacy of whole-brain radiotherapy to people with multiple brain metastases, unless as part of a clinical trial.

mcqs.question: A patient asks about memantine alongside whole-brain radiotherapy for multiple brain metastases. What's the NICE position?

options.A: Offer if hippocampal avoidance isn't available
options.C: Only as part of a clinical trial
options.D: Offer to all to protect cognition
options.E: Offer for the first 4 weeks only

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Only as part of a clinical trial
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer memantine in addition to WBRT to people with multiple brain metastases unless as part of a clinical trial.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer memantine in addition to whole-brain radiotherapy to people with multiple brain metastases, unless as part of a clinical trial.

mcqs.question: Which follow-up imaging does NICE recommend for people with known or resected brain metastases?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2022): offer brain MRI for follow-up imaging instead of brain CE-CT.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer brain MRI for follow-up imaging, instead of brain CE-CT, to people with known or resected brain metastases. [2022]

mcqs.question: A patient has radiologically suspected brain metastases that may be suitable for focal treatment. Which additional investigation does NICE recommend to establish disease status?

options.B: Repeat brain CT at 6 weeks to confirm the lesions are metastatic
options.E: Extracranial imaging suited to the primary

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Extracranial imaging suited to the primary
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer extracranial imaging appropriate to the primary tumour type to help establish current disease status.

sourceRefs.excerpt: To help establish current disease status, offer extracranial imaging (appropriate to the primary tumour type) to people with any radiologically suspected brain metastases that may be suitable for focal treatment.

mcqs.question: For which brain metastases does NICE suggest considering systemic anticancer therapy, because they're likely to respond effectively?

options.A: All metastases from any primary, regardless of the expected response
options.D: Germ cell tumours or small-cell lung cancer

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Germ cell tumours or small-cell lung cancer
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider systemic anticancer therapy for brain metastases likely to respond effectively, e.g. germ cell tumours or small-cell lung cancer.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider systemic anti-cancer therapy for people who have brain metastases likely to respond effectively, for example, germ cell tumours or small-cell lung cancer.

mcqs.question: According to ASCO-SNO-ASTRO (2022), which patients with brain metastases are more likely to benefit from surgery?
mcqs.explanation: ASCO-SNO-ASTRO: patients with large tumours with mass effect are more likely to benefit than those with multiple metastases and/or uncontrolled systemic disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Surgery is a reasonable option for patients with brain metastases, particularly for those with large tumors causing mass effect, as they are more likely to benefit.
Patients with large tumors with mass effect are more likely to benefit from surgery than those with multiple brain metastases and/or uncontrolled systemic disease.

mcqs.question: What does ASCO-SNO-ASTRO (2022) recommend for patients with symptomatic brain metastases?
mcqs.explanation: ASCO-SNO-ASTRO: patients with symptomatic brain metastases should receive local therapy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Patients with symptomatic brain metastases should receive local therapy.

mcqs.question: Which advanced radiotherapy techniques does ASTRO (2022) say should be considered for brain metastases?

options.A: Conventional opposed lateral whole-brain fields with no hippocampal sparing

mcqs.explanation: ASTRO 2022: advanced techniques such as SRS and hippocampal avoidance WBRT should be considered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Advanced radiation therapy techniques such as stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and hippocampal avoidance whole brain radiation therapy should be considered in the management of patients with brain metastases.

mcqs.question: In the 2016 trial of SRS alone versus SRS plus WBRT, what was the incidence of cognitive deterioration at 3 months among long-term survivors?

options.A: 94.1% with SRS alone vs 45.5% with WBRT
options.C: 45.5% with SRS alone vs 94.1% with WBRT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: 45.5% with SRS alone vs 94.1% with WBRT
mcqs.explanation: Long-term survivors had less cognitive deterioration with SRS alone at 3 months (45.5% vs 94.1%) and 12 months (60% vs 94.4%).

sourceRefs.excerpt: For long-term survivors, the incidence of cognitive deterioration was less after SRS alone at 3 months (5/11 [45.5%] vs 16/17 [94.1%]; difference, -48.7%; 95% CI, -87.6% to -9.7%; P = .007) and at 12 months (6/10 [60%] vs 17/18 [94.4%]; difference, -34.4%; 95% CI, -74.4% to 5.5%; P = .04). mcqs.question: In the 2011 trial of WBRT after surgery or radiosurgery for limited brain metastases, how did WBRT change the 2-year relapse rate at initial sites after surgery?
mcqs.explanation: WBRT reduced the 2-year relapse rate at initial sites after surgery from 59% to 27%.

sourceRefs.excerpt: WBRT reduced the 2-year relapse rate both at initial sites (surgery: 59% to 27%, P Conclusion After radiosurgery or surgery of a limi

mcqs.question: A patient with melanoma has brain metastases that might be suitable for surgery or stereotactic radiotherapy. Where does NICE recommend referral?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2015, amended 2022): refer to the neuro-oncology MDT for a treatment recommendation.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Refer people with melanoma and brain metastases that might be suitable for surgery or stereotactic radiotherapy to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team for a recommendation about treatment. [2015, amended 2022]

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend for ongoing follow-up of people with brain metastases, beyond imaging?

options.A: Regular physical, psychological and cognitive review
options.B: Cognitive testing only before treatment, with no later clinical reassessment

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Regular physical, psychological and cognitive review
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer regular clinical review to assess changes in physical, psychological and cognitive wellbeing.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer regular clinical review for people with brain metastases to assess changes in their physical, psychological and cognitive wellbeing.

mcqs.question: Which MRI protocol does NICE describe as standard structural MRI for reviewing brain metastases?

options.A: Diffusion tensor imaging and perfusion only, without contrast sequences

mcqs.explanation: NICE: standard structural MRI is T2-weighted, FLAIR, DWI series and T1 pre- and post-contrast volume.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider standard structural MRI (defined as T2 weighted, FLAIR, DWI series and T1 pre- and post-contrast volume) as part of regular clinical review for people with brain metastases, to assess for progression or recurrence, unless MRI is contraindicated.

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest considering referral for neurological rehabilitation assessment in a person with a brain tumour?

options.B: Only in the last year of life
options.C: Only after completing radiotherapy, once acute side effects have settled
options.D: At diagnosis and every stage of follow-up

mcqs.correctAnswerText: At diagnosis and every stage of follow-up
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider referral for neurological rehabilitation assessment of physical, cognitive and emotional function at diagnosis and every stage of follow-up.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider referring the person with a brain tumour for a neurological rehabilitation assessment of physical, cognitive and emotional function at diagnosis and every stage of follow‑up.

mcqs.question: What's the typical median overall survival from diagnosis of brain metastases in metastatic melanoma, as stated in the 2012 dabrafenib trial background?
mcqs.explanation: The trial background states median OS from diagnosis of melanoma brain metastases is typically 17–22 weeks.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Background Brain metastases are common in patients with metastatic melanoma and median overall survival from their diagnosis is typically 17-22 weeks. We assessed dabrafenib in patients with Val600Glu or Val600Lys BRAF-mutant melanoma metastatic to the brain. Methods We undertook a mu

mcqs.question: A pregnant woman has stage IIB–IV melanoma. Which staging imaging does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2022): offer whole-body and brain MRI, instead of CE-CT, to women with stage IIB–IV melanoma who are pregnant.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer staging with whole body and brain MRI, instead of CE-CT, to: children and young adults (from birth to 24 years) with stage IIB to IV melanoma; women with stage IIB to IV melanoma who are pregnant. [2022]

mcqs.question: A 62-year-old with advanced Parkinson's disease has disabling symptoms despite best medical therapy. Which surgical option does NICE suggest considering?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2017): consider deep brain stimulation for advanced PD whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by best medical therapy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider deep brain stimulation for people with advanced Parkinson's disease whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by best medical therapy. [2017]

mcqs.question: Before DBS is considered in advanced Parkinson's disease, which treatments does NICE include in best medical therapy?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer best medical therapy for advanced PD, which may include intermittent apomorphine injection and/or continuous subcutaneous apomorphine infusion.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer people with advanced Parkinson's disease best medical therapy, which may include intermittent apomorphine injection and/or continuous subcutaneous apomorphine infusion. [2017]

mcqs.question: An adult with cerebral palsy has severe painful dystonia despite enteral anti-dystonic drugs and botulinum toxin. What does NICE suggest?

options.A: Referral to a specialised DBS centre
options.B: Repeat botulinum toxin injections every 2 weeks at escalating doses

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Referral to a specialised DBS centre
mcqs.explanation: NICE: if severe painful dystonia persists despite enteral drugs or botulinum toxin A, consider referral to a specialised centre experienced in DBS.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If adults with cerebral palsy continue to have severe and painful dystonia, despite having enteral anti-dystonic drug treatment or botulinum toxin type A treatment, consider referring them to a specialised centre with experience in providing deep brain stimulation. See also NICE interventional procedures guidance on deep brain stimulation for tremor and dystonia (excluding Parkinson's disease) .

mcqs.question: A person with Parkinson's disease has dyskinesia and motor fluctuations despite optimal levodopa. Which adjunct options does NICE recommend offering a choice from?

options.B: Ergot agonist as the only option
options.D: Dopamine agonist, MAO-B or COMT inhibitor

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Dopamine agonist, MAO-B or COMT inhibitor
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer a choice of dopamine agonists, MAO-B inhibitors or COMT inhibitors as adjuncts after discussing individual circumstances.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer a choice of dopamine agonists, MAO‑B inhibitors or catechol‑O‑methyl transferase (COMT) inhibitors as an adjunct to levodopa for people with Parkinson's disease who have developed dyskinesia or motor fluctuations despite optimal levodopa therapy, after discussing: the person's individual clinical circumstances, for example, their Parkinson's disease symptoms, comorbidities and risks from polypharmacy; the person's individual lifestyle circumstances, preferences, needs and goals; the potent

mcqs.question: Which drug class does NICE advise against for people with PD who have developed dyskinesia or motor fluctuations?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer anticholinergics to people with PD who have developed dyskinesia and/or motor fluctuations.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer anticholinergics to people with Parkinson's disease who have developed dyskinesia and/or motor fluctuations. [2017]

mcqs.question: When does NICE allow an ergot-derived dopamine agonist to be considered in PD?

options.C: As first-line monotherapy in early disease, to delay starting levodopa
options.E: As adjunct after non-ergot agonists fail

mcqs.correctAnswerText: As adjunct after non-ergot agonists fail
mcqs.explanation: NICE: only consider ergot agonists as adjuncts to levodopa in people with dyskinesia/fluctuations whose symptoms aren't controlled by a non-ergot agonist; never first-line.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Only consider an ergot-derived dopamine agonist as an adjunct to levodopa for people with Parkinson's disease: who have developed dyskinesia or motor fluctuations despite optimal levodopa therapy and whose symptoms are not adequately controlled with a non-ergot-derived dopamine agonist. [2017] Follow the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency guidance on the warnings and contraindications for ergot-derived dopamine agonists .

Do not offer ergot-derived dopamine agonists as first-line treatment for Parkinson's disease. [2017] Follow the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency guidance on the warnings and contraindications for ergot-derived dopamine agonists .

mcqs.question: A person in the early stages of PD has motor symptoms affecting their quality of life. What does NICE recommend offering?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2017): offer levodopa to people in early PD whose motor symptoms impact on their quality of life.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer levodopa to people in the early stages of Parkinson's disease whose motor symptoms impact on their quality of life. [2017]

mcqs.question: Early PD symptoms aren't yet affecting quality of life. Which options does NICE suggest considering?

options.B: Dopamine agonist, levodopa or MAO-B inhibitor
options.D: Only an ergot-derived dopamine agonist, started at diagnosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Dopamine agonist, levodopa or MAO-B inhibitor
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider a choice of dopamine agonists, levodopa or MAO-B inhibitors for early PD whose motor symptoms don't impact quality of life.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider a choice of dopamine agonists, levodopa or monoamine oxidase B (MAO‑B) inhibitors for people in the early stages of Parkinson's disease whose motor symptoms do not impact on their quality of life. [2017]

mcqs.question: Parkinson's disease is suspected in primary care. What does NICE recommend?

options.A: Refer quickly and untreated to a specialist
options.B: Do a levodopa challenge test first
options.C: Start levodopa and refer if no response
options.D: Arrange structural MRI to confirm the diagnosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Refer quickly and untreated to a specialist
mcqs.explanation: NICE: if PD is suspected, refer quickly and untreated to a specialist in the differential diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If Parkinson's disease is suspected, refer people quickly and untreated to a specialist with expertise in the differential diagnosis of this condition. [2006, amended 2017]

mcqs.question: Which statement about structural MRI in Parkinson's disease is consistent with NICE?

options.C: It's the first-line diagnostic test and should precede specialist referral
options.D: It confirms PD in most cases
options.E: It shouldn't be used to diagnose PD

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It shouldn't be used to diagnose PD
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not use structural MRI to diagnose PD.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not use structural MRI to diagnose Parkinson's disease. [2006, amended 2017]

mcqs.question: How often does NICE say people diagnosed with PD should be seen to review the diagnosis?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: review the diagnosis regularly, at intervals of 6 to 12 months, and reconsider if atypical features develop.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Review the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease regularly, and reconsider it if atypical clinical features develop. (People diagnosed with Parkinson's disease should be seen at regular intervals of 6 to 12 months to review their diagnosis.) [2006]

mcqs.question: A person with PD is admitted to hospital. What does NICE advise about their antiparkinsonian medicines?

options.A: Convert all doses to once daily
options.B: Give on time; adjust only with a PD specialist
options.D: Stop them while the patient is nil by mouth, and restart after discharge
options.E: Withhold until the medical team reviews

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Give on time; adjust only with a PD specialist
mcqs.explanation: NICE: because of the risks of sudden changes, give medicines at the appropriate times (sometimes self-medication) and adjust only with a PD specialist.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In view of the risks of sudden changes in antiparkinsonian medicines, people with Parkinson's disease who are admitted to hospital or care homes should have their medicines: given at the appropriate times, which in some cases may mean allowing self-medication; adjusted by, or adjusted only after discussion with, a specialist in the management of Parkinson's disease. [2006]

mcqs.question: A person with PD has hallucinations that they and their family tolerate well. What does NICE advise?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not treat hallucinations and delusions that are well tolerated by the person and their family or carers.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not treat hallucinations and delusions if they are well tolerated by the person with Parkinson's disease and their family members and carers (as appropriate). [2017]

mcqs.question: Distressing psychosis in PD hasn't responded to standard treatment. Which drug does NICE recommend offering?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: if standard treatment isn't effective, offer clozapine for hallucinations and delusions; registration with a monitoring service is needed.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If standard treatment is not effective, offer clozapine to treat hallucinations and delusions in people with Parkinson's disease. Be aware that registration with a patient monitoring service is needed. [2017]

mcqs.question: Which antipsychotic does NICE suggest considering for hallucinations in PD without cognitive impairment?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider quetiapine to treat hallucinations and delusions in PD with no cognitive impairment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider quetiapine to treat hallucinations and delusions in people with Parkinson's disease who have no cognitive impairment. [2017]

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend for people with mild or moderate Parkinson's disease dementia?
mcqs.explanation: NICE (2017): offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for mild or moderate PD dementia (rivastigmine capsules were then the licensed option).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for people with mild or moderate Parkinson's disease dementia. [2017] In July 2017, rivastigmine capsules are the only treatment with a UK marketing authorisation for this indication. Use of donepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine patches was off-label. See NICE's information on prescribing medicines .

mcqs.question: Which drug does NICE suggest considering for orthostatic hypotension in PD, with monitoring for supine hypertension?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider midodrine for PD with orthostatic hypotension, taking into account contraindications and monitoring requirements.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider midodrine for people with Parkinson's disease and orthostatic hypotension, taking into account the contraindications and monitoring requirements (including monitoring for supine hypertension). [2017]

mcqs.question: What dietary advice about protein does NICE give to people with PD?

options.B: Avoid all dietary protein at lunch
options.D: Use protein shakes with every levodopa dose

mcqs.explanation: NICE: advise people with PD to avoid a reduction in their total daily protein consumption.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Advise people with Parkinson's disease to avoid a reduction in their total daily protein consumption. [2017]

mcqs.question: Which treatment does NICE suggest considering for nocturnal akinesia in PD?

options.D: Continuous apomorphine infusion as first-line treatment
options.E: Levodopa or an oral dopamine agonist

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Levodopa or an oral dopamine agonist
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider levodopa or oral dopamine agonists for nocturnal akinesia; if one isn't effective or tolerated, offer the other.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider levodopa or oral dopamine agonists to treat nocturnal akinesia in people with Parkinson's disease. If the selected option is not effective or not tolerated, offer the other instead. [2017]

mcqs.question: Which therapy does NICE recommend offering for PD-related balance or motor function problems?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer PD-specific physiotherapy for people experiencing balance or motor function problems; the Alexander Technique may also be considered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer Parkinson's disease-specific physiotherapy for people who are experiencing balance or motor function problems. [2017]
Consider the Alexander Technique for people with Parkinson's disease who are experiencing balance or motor function problems. [2017]

mcqs.question: A patient with MSCC isn't suitable for spinal surgery, has had partial weakness for 2 days and has a reasonable prognosis. What does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer urgent radiotherapy (as soon as possible, within 24 hours) for MSCC not suitable for surgery, unless complete plegia ≥2 weeks with controlled pain or poor prognosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer urgent radiotherapy (to be given as soon as possible and within 24 hours) to people with MSCC that is not suitable for spinal surgery, unless: they have had complete tetraplegia or paraplegia for 2 weeks or longer and their pain is well controlled or their overall prognosis is considered to be poor (see also the section on tools for assessing spinal stability and prognosis ). [2023]

mcqs.question: Which patient with MSCC meets NICE's exception criteria for urgent radiotherapy?

options.A: Ambulant with radicular pain and no motor deficit, with a good prognosis
options.C: New back pain with sensory level

mcqs.explanation: NICE exceptions: complete tetraplegia or paraplegia for 2 weeks or longer with well-controlled pain, or poor overall prognosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer urgent radiotherapy (to be given as soon as possible and within 24 hours) to people with MSCC that is not suitable for spinal surgery, unless: they have had complete tetraplegia or paraplegia for 2 weeks or longer and their pain is well controlled or their overall prognosis is considered to be poor (see also the section on tools for assessing spinal stability and prognosis ). [2023]

mcqs.question: A patient with MSCC has spinal instability and mechanical pain not controlled by analgesia, with a severe neurological deficit that may be irreversible. They're fit for surgery. What does NICE recommend?

options.A: Radiotherapy only, because the deficit is irreversible

mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer stabilisation surgery even if there's a severe and possibly irreversible deficit, if there's instability with uncontrolled mechanical pain and the person can have surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer spinal stabilisation surgery, even if there is a severe neurological deficit that may be irreversible, if a person with MSCC: has suspected or confirmed spinal instability with mechanical pain that is not controlled by analgesia and is able to have surgery and it is suitable for them. [2023]

mcqs.question: A patient with MSCC has instability and uncontrolled mechanical pain but isn't suitable for surgery. What does NICE recommend?

options.C: Epidural steroid injection at the level of instability for pain control
options.E: External spinal support, e.g. halo or CTLO

mcqs.correctAnswerText: External spinal support, e.g. halo or CTLO
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer external spinal support (halo vest or cervico-thoraco-lumbar orthosis) when surgery isn't suitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer external spinal support (for example, a halo vest or cervico-thoraco-lumbar orthosis) if a person with MSCC: has suspected or confirmed spinal instability with mechanical pain that is not controlled by analgesia and surgery is not suitable for them. [2023]

mcqs.question: What did the 2005 randomised trial (Patchell) show for MSCC?

options.B: RT alone beat surgery plus RT

mcqs.explanation: Direct decompressive surgery plus postoperative radiotherapy was superior to radiotherapy alone, with less need for corticosteroids and opioids.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The need for corticosteroids and opioid analgesics was significantly reduced in the surgical group. Interpretation Direct decompressive surgery plus postoperative radiotherapy is superior to treatment with radiotherapy alone for patients with spinal cord compression caused by metastatic cancer.

mcqs.question: After surgery for MSCC, what does NICE recommend once the patient has recovered?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer postoperative radiotherapy after the person has recovered from surgery for spinal metastases or MSCC.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer postoperative radiotherapy after the person has recovered from surgery for spinal metastases or MSCC. For information on surgery, see the section on invasive interventions . [2023]

mcqs.question: Which imaging approach to suspected spinal metastases or MSCC does NICE advise against?

options.A: Plain spinal X-ray to diagnose or exclude
options.E: Myelography at a neuroscience or spinal surgical centre when indicated

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Plain spinal X-ray to diagnose or exclude
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not do a plain X-ray of the spine to diagnose or rule out spinal metastases or MSCC.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not do a plain X-ray of the spine to diagnose or rule out spinal metastases or MSCC. [2023]

mcqs.question: A patient with suspected MSCC can't have MRI. What does NICE recommend?

options.B: Isotope bone scan alone, followed by a repeat scan at 6 weeks
options.E: CT, with myelography rarely if needed

mcqs.correctAnswerText: CT, with myelography rarely if needed
mcqs.explanation: NICE: if MRI is contraindicated, do CT. Rarely, myelography after CT if more information is needed, and only at a neuroscience/spinal centre.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If MRI is contraindicated, carry out a CT scan for people with suspected spinal metastases or MSCC. Rarely, if more information is needed for diagnosis and to guide management, carry out myelography after CT scanning. [2023]
If myelography is indicated, only do it at a neuroscience or spinal surgical centre. [2023]

mcqs.question: Clinical suspicion of spinal metastases exists but there's no suspicion of MSCC. What MRI timing does NICE recommend?

options.D: Within 1 week at the local hospital

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Within 1 week at the local hospital
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer MRI to guide treatment within 1 week at the local hospital.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer an MRI scan to guide treatment options for people with clinical suspicion of spinal metastases but without suspicion of MSCC (see recommendation 1.3.3 ), to be done: within 1 week; at the local hospital. [2023]

mcqs.question: A patient with known spinal metastases has no symptoms or signs of cord compression. What does NICE say about MRI surveillance?

options.B: No MRI solely for early detection

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No MRI solely for early detection
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not do spinal MRI solely for early radiological detection of cord compression in asymptomatic people with spinal metastases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In people with an existing diagnosis of spinal metastases without symptoms or signs of cord compression, do not do MRI of the spine solely for the early radiological detection of cord compression. [2023]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest radiotherapy for asymptomatic spinal metastases?

options.E: Routinely for all asymptomatic spinal metastases, to prevent MSCC

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider RT only in an RCT, as part of an oligometastatic strategy (up to 3 metastases), or if there are radiological signs of impending cord compression.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with asymptomatic spinal metastases, consider radiotherapy only: as part of a randomised controlled trial with the intention of preventing MSCC or as part of a treatment strategy for oligometastases (up to 3 discrete metastases anywhere in the body) with spinal involvement or if there are radiological signs of impending cord compression by an epidural or intradural tumour. [2023]

mcqs.question: A patient with spinal metastases without MSCC has spinal instability and uncontrolled pain. Which interventions does NICE suggest considering?

options.D: Spinal fusion, offered only as part of a randomised controlled trial

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty, radiofrequency ablation and other options, alone or in combination.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with spinal metastases without MSCC who have suspected or confirmed spinal instability, or pain not controlled by analgesia, consider the following options alone or in combination: vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty (see also NICE's interventional procedures guidance on percutaneous vertebroplasty and balloon kyphoplasty for vertebral compression fractures ); radiofrequency ablation (see also NICE's interventional procedures guidance on radiofrequency ablation for palliation of painful spi

mcqs.question: Which validated scoring system does NICE give as an example to inform spinal stability decisions?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider a validated spinal stability score with good evidence of accuracy, e.g. SINS, alongside clinical assessment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider using a validated spinal stability scoring system with good evidence of accuracy (for example, the Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score) alongside clinical assessment of risk of spinal instability to inform treatment decisions. [2023]

mcqs.question: Imaging suggests the spine is likely to be stable. How does NICE suggest stability is tested?

options.E: Immediate full mobilisation without any graded assessment beforehand

mcqs.explanation: NICE: if spinal stability is likely, start testing by graded sitting followed by weight bearing.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If assessment, including imaging, suggests spinal stability is likely (before or after treatment), start testing this by graded sitting followed by weight bearing. [2023]

mcqs.question: Dexamethasone was given before imaging, and MSCC and spinal metastases were then excluded. What does NICE advise?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: if spinal metastases and MSCC are ruled out, discontinue dexamethasone.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If dexamethasone is given before imaging, and spinal metastases and MSCC are subsequently ruled out, discontinue it. [2023]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest corticosteroids for people with spinal metastases or MSCC without neurological symptoms or signs?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider corticosteroids without neurology if there is severe pain or a haematological malignancy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider giving corticosteroids as part of initial management to people with spinal metastases or MSCC who do not have neurological symptoms or signs, if they have: severe pain or a haematological malignancy (see recommendation 1.8.5). [2023]

mcqs.question: For which tumour types does NICE recommend bisphosphonates to reduce pain and the risk of vertebral fracture or collapse?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer bisphosphonates for spinal involvement from myeloma or breast cancer. For prostate cancer, only if conventional analgesia fails.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with spinal involvement from myeloma or breast cancer, offer bisphosphonates to reduce pain and the risk of vertebral fracture or collapse. [2008]

Do not use bisphosphonates to treat spinal pain in people: with vertebral involvement from tumour types other than myeloma, breast cancer or prostate cancer (if conventional analgesia fails) or with the intention of preventing MSCC, except as part of a randomised controlled trial. [2008]

mcqs.question: When should early expert advice be sought and spinal stability assessment started, according to NICE?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: seek early advice (within 24 hours) from an expert and start stability assessment to minimise immobilisation.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Seek early advice (within 24 hours) from an expert healthcare professional (for example, a specialist physiotherapist, oncologist or spinal surgeon) and start assessment of spinal stability to minimise the duration of immobilisation, if appropriate. [2023]

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest considering further radiotherapy for spinal metastases or MSCC?

options.B: Good prior response; symptoms recur ≥3 months later
options.C: Recurrence of pain within 2 weeks of first RT, regardless of initial response
options.D: Any persistent pain during first RT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Good prior response; symptoms recur ≥3 months later
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider further RT for people with a good response to previous RT who develop recurrent symptoms at least 3 months after initial RT.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider further radiotherapy for people with spinal metastases or MSCC who have: had a good response to previous radiotherapy and developed recurrent symptoms at least 3 months after initial radiotherapy. [2023]

mcqs.question: According to DEGRO (2009), what's a preferred standard palliative treatment for MSCC in breast cancer?
mcqs.explanation: DEGRO 2009: radiation therapy is a preferred standard palliative treatment for MSCC in breast cancer patients.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For metastatic spinal cord compression (MSCC) in breast cancer patients, radiation therapy is a preferred standard palliative treatment.

topics.topicKey: pertussis clinical stages macrolide treatment post-exposure prophylaxis vaccination

topics.coverageNote: FLAGGED SHORT (12 Qs): there are no stored rows on pertussis clinical stages (catarrhal/paroxysmal/convalescent), macrolide treatment, or post-exposure prophylaxis. mcqs.question: Which statement reflects the ACIP (2018) recommendation on pertussis vaccination in children?

options.B: Infants and young children should be vaccinated
options.E: Vaccination only during local outbreaks, after a confirmed case in the area

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Infants and young children should be vaccinated
mcqs.explanation: ACIP 2018: infants and young children are recommended to receive pertussis vaccination. Routine Td/pertussis vaccination is also recommended.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Infants and young children are recommended to receive pertussis vaccination.
Routine vaccination for tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis is recommended.

mcqs.question: By how much has pertussis vaccination reduced notified cases in industrialised countries from peak years, according to the 2007 trial background?
mcqs.explanation: Pertussis vaccination has reduced notified cases in industrialised countries from peak years by more than 95%.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Background Pertussis vaccination has reduced the number of notified cases in industrialized countries from peak years by more than 95%.

mcqs.question: In October 2011, what did ACIP recommend about Tdap for pregnant women?

options.A: Postpartum vaccination only, because vaccination during pregnancy is avoided
options.E: All pregnant women should routinely receive Tdap

mcqs.correctAnswerText: All pregnant women should routinely receive Tdap
mcqs.explanation: ACIP's updated recommendation: all pregnant women routinely receive a dose of Tdap. VAERS reports after this change were later characterised.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Background In October 2011, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) issued updated recommendations that all pregnant women routinely receive a dose of tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccine. Objectives We characterized reports to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) in pregnant women who received Tdap after thi

mcqs.question: At a pregnant woman's first appointment after the 20-week scan, what does NICE advise antenatal care providers to check?

options.D: Whether pertussis vaccine was offered and accepted
options.E: Whether influenza vaccination was given during the first trimester of pregnancy

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Whether pertussis vaccine was offered and accepted
mcqs.explanation: NICE: check whether she has been offered and accepted pertussis vaccination in this pregnancy. If not, ensure offers or reminders follow at later contacts.

sourceRefs.excerpt: At a pregnant woman's first appointment after the 20‑week scan, antenatal care providers should check whether they have been offered and accepted vaccination against pertussis in this pregnancy. If not, ensure they receive offers of vaccination or reminders (as relevant) at subsequent antenatal appointments or during any contact with their GP, midwife, health visitor or any other healthcare provider.

mcqs.question: Who does NICE say should offer pertussis vaccination to pregnant women during routine antenatal visits?

options.B: Midwives, or signpost if they can't give it
options.E: Only health visitors, after birth, at the new baby review

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Midwives, or signpost if they can't give it
mcqs.explanation: NICE: midwives should offer vaccination during routine antenatal visits per the Green Book schedule. If they can't administer it, they should signpost to vaccination services.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Midwives should offer vaccination to pregnant women during routine antenatal visits, as recommended by the Green book and the NHS routine UK immunisation schedule . If the midwife cannot administer the vaccine, they should signpost women to vaccination services, drop-in clinics or their GP practice.

mcqs.question: Which vaccine co-administration with Tdap is described as recommended in US adolescents (2011 trial)?
mcqs.explanation: In the US, co-administration of Tdap and MCV4 is recommended in adolescents.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In the United States, co-administration of tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccine and tetravalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine (MCV4) is recommended in adolescents.

mcqs.question: Which investigational vaccine was assessed when given concomitantly with Tdap in people aged 11–25 years (2010 trial)?
mcqs.explanation: The 2010 study evaluated the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of MenACWY-CRM given concomitantly with Tdap in people aged 11–25 years.

sourceRefs.excerpt: This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of an investigational quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine, MenACWY-CRM, when administered concomitantly with a combined tetanus, reduced diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccine, in subjects aged 11 to 25 years.

mcqs.question: What does Pediatrics (2017) say about adolescent healthcare visits and pertussis-containing vaccination?

options.A: Tdap should only be given at age 18
options.B: Adolescent boosters aren't needed if the infant primary course was completed
options.C: Only school visits should be used
options.D: Every visit is a chance to update Tdap

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Every visit is a chance to update Tdap
mcqs.explanation: Every adolescent visit should be viewed as an opportunity to update and complete immunisations, including Tdap.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Every adolescent visit should be viewed as an opportunity to update and complete an adolescent's immunizations, including tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis vaccine.

mcqs.question: Which healthcare practitioners does NICE say should ensure pregnant women are invited for vaccination or signposted to services?

options.A: Maternity and others in contact with them
options.E: Only school nurses, during routine school-aged immunisation sessions

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Maternity and others in contact with them
mcqs.explanation: NICE: practitioners in maternity services and other healthcare practitioners in contact with pregnant women should ensure invitation or signposting.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Practitioners working in maternity services and other healthcare practitioners who have contact with pregnant women should ensure that pregnant women are invited for vaccination or signposted to vaccination services or drop-in clinics.

mcqs.question: A child remains unvaccinated after 3 invitations from the GP practice. What does NICE say the practice should do?

options.A: Remove the child from the practice list
options.B: Inform the child health information service
options.C: Refer to a paediatric outpatient clinic
options.E: Report to social services immediately as a safeguarding concern

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Inform the child health information service
mcqs.explanation: NICE: GP practices should inform CHIS if 3 invitations are made but a child remains unvaccinated.

sourceRefs.excerpt: GP practices should inform CHIS if 3 invitations for vaccination are made but a child remains unvaccinated (see recommendation 1.3.16 ).

mcqs.question: A parent declines a pertussis-containing vaccine for their child. What does NICE advise?

options.B: Remove the child from the practice
options.D: Re-offer it at the same visit, repeatedly, until the parent accepts
options.E: Record it with the reason; explain later access

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Record it with the reason; explain later access
mcqs.explanation: NICE: record the decline with the reason, if given, and make sure they know how to get vaccinated later if they change their mind.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If someone declines an offer of vaccination, record this with the reason why, if given, and make sure they know how to get a vaccination at a later date if they change their mind.

mcqs.question: Within what timeframe does NICE say vaccinations should be reported to GP practices and CHIS?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: report vaccinations promptly, within 5 working days or in line with stricter standards, to GP practices and CHIS.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Providers should ensure that vaccinations are reported promptly (within 5 working days, or in line with required standards if shorter) to GP practices and child health information services (CHIS) (if relevant).

mcqs.question: What does the Endocrine Society (2010) recommend for detecting severe 21-hydroxylase deficiency?

options.C: Screening only siblings of known cases, after genetic confirmation in the index case

mcqs.explanation: Endocrine Society 2010: universal newborn screening for severe 21-OH deficiency, followed by confirmatory tests.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Recommend universal newborn screening for severe steroid 21-hydroxylase deficiency followed by confirmatory tests.

mcqs.question: What proportion of CAH cases are due to disorders of 21-hydroxylation, and what's the inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: CAH is a group of autosomal recessive disorders of adrenal steroidogenesis. 21-hydroxylation defects account for over 95%.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is a group of autosomal recessive disorders of adrenal steroidogenesis. Disorders in steroid 21-hydroxylation account for over 95% of patients with CAH. Clinically, the 21-hydroxylase deficiency has been classified in a broad spectrum of clinical forms, ranging f

mcqs.question: What dosing principle does the Endocrine Society (2010) emphasise for glucocorticoids in CAH?

options.A: Double the dose at puberty for all
options.C: Fix the dose regardless of growth
options.E: Use the minimum dose, to avoid iatrogenic Cushing's

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Use the minimum dose, to avoid iatrogenic Cushing's
mcqs.explanation: Endocrine Society: minimise glucocorticoid dosage to avoid iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome in CAH.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Minimize glucocorticoid dosage to avoid iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome in CAH patients.

mcqs.question: How does JCEM (2018) say glucocorticoid replacement should be approached in 21-hydroxylase deficiency CAH?
mcqs.explanation: JCEM 2018: glucocorticoid replacement therapy should be individualised for CAH due to 21-OH deficiency.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
sourceRefs.excerpt: Glucocorticoid replacement therapy should be individualized for patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

mcqs.question: What's often blamed for inadequate final height in CAH (J Pediatr Endocrinol Metab 2001)?

options.C: Untreated mineralocorticoid deficiency alone, independent of glucocorticoid dose
options.D: GC overtreatment and poor androgen control

mcqs.correctAnswerText: GC overtreatment and poor androgen control
mcqs.explanation: Inadequate final height is often attributed to glucocorticoid overtreatment and poor control of adrenal androgens.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
sourceRefs.excerpt: Inadequate final height in CAH patients is often attributed to overtreatment with glucocorticoid replacement and poor control of adrenal androgen levels.

mcqs.question: What does the An Pediatr (2017) guidance say about genetic study in 21-hydroxylase-deficient CAH?

options.A: It should be avoided in children
options.B: It isn't useful once the biochemical diagnosis has already been confirmed
options.E: It's essential for diagnosis, counselling and prenatal diagnosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It's essential for diagnosis, counselling and prenatal diagnosis
mcqs.explanation: Patient and family genetic study is essential for diagnosis and allows genetic counselling and prenatal diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A patient and family genetic study is essential for the diagnosis of the patient, and allows genetic counselling, as well as a prenatal diagnosis for 21-hydroxylase-deficient congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

mcqs.question: What treatment approach does An Pediatr (2017) recommend for classic forms of 21-hydroxylase-deficient CAH?

options.B: Deferred treatment until puberty, to avoid early growth suppression

mcqs.explanation: An early and appropriate individualised treatment is recommended for classic forms.

sourceRefs.excerpt: An early and appropriate individualized treatment is recommended for classic forms of 21-hydroxylase-deficient congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

mcqs.question: Why are many women with nonclassic 21-hydroxylase deficiency (NCAH) at risk of having infants with classic CAH?

options.D: They often carry a severe CYP21 mutation allele
options.E: NCAH always converts to classic CAH in pregnancy

mcqs.correctAnswerText: They often carry a severe CYP21 mutation allele
mcqs.explanation: Many women with NCAH carry at least one allele with a severe CYP21 mutation, so they're at risk of a child with classic CAH.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Context Because many women with 21-hydroxylase (21-OH)-deficient nonclassic adrenal hyperplasia (NCAH) carry at least one allele affected by a severe mutation of CYP21, they are at risk for giving birth to infants with classic adrenal hyperplasia (CAH). Objective Our objective was to

mcqs.question: What replacement does NICE recommend for people with congenital adrenal hyperplasia?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoid (if needed) for primary AI or CAH. Glucocorticoids alone for secondary/tertiary AI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoid (if needed) for people with primary adrenal insufficiency or congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Offer glucocorticoids alone for people with secondary and tertiary adrenal insufficiency .

mcqs.question: How often does NICE recommend appointments for children under 16 with adrenal insufficiency, including CAH?

options.A: Every 3 months by telephone only, with no physical measurements

mcqs.explanation: NICE: at least every 6 months, with a face-to-face review at least annually to measure height and weight and adjust doses.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer children and young people under 16 years an appointment at least every 6 months and a face-to-face review at least annually to measure their height and weight and adjust glucocorticoid (and mineralocorticoid for primary adrenal insufficiency ) dose accordingly.

mcqs.question: A pregnant woman with CAH reaches the third trimester. What does NICE suggest about her replacement doses?

options.B: Switch to dexamethasone, because it crosses the placenta less readily
options.E: Consider increasing according to symptoms, Na and BP

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Consider increasing according to symptoms, Na and BP
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider increasing glucocorticoid (and mineralocorticoid) doses in the third trimester if needed, based on symptoms, sodium and postural BP.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider increasing glucocorticoid (and mineralocorticoid for primary adrenal insufficiency) replacement doses in the third trimester of pregnancy, if needed, depending on clinical symptoms, sodium levels and postural blood pressure.

mcqs.question: Who should monitor a pregnant woman with adrenal insufficiency, according to NICE?

options.D: Endocrinology only, with the first review after delivery

mcqs.explanation: NICE: monitoring during pregnancy should be done by a multidisciplinary team experienced in managing adrenal insufficiency in pregnancy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Monitoring during pregnancy should be done by a multidisciplinary team experienced in managing adrenal insufficiency during pregnancy.

mcqs.question: Which monitoring tests does NICE recommend for adults with adrenal insufficiency, including CAH?

options.B: Annual cortisol day curve to titrate the hydrocortisone dose precisely
options.D: Lying/standing BP, electrolytes, HbA1c, bone density

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Lying/standing BP, electrolytes, HbA1c, bone density
mcqs.explanation: NICE: lying and standing BP, electrolytes, HbA1c, bone density (adults, at least once in 5 years after diagnosis), and a lipid profile.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer the following measurements and tests to people with adrenal insufficiency and use the results to aid decision making: blood pressure (lying and standing); electrolytes; HbA1c; bone density (for adults at least once in the 5 years after diagnosis); lipid profile (for adults).

mcqs.question: A person with primary adrenal insufficiency has persistent hyponatraemia despite maximum fludrocortisone. What does NICE suggest?

options.E: Doubling the hydrocortisone dose long-term to correct the sodium

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider sodium chloride supplementation according to specialist endocrinology advice.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For people with primary adrenal insufficiency and persistent hyponatraemia despite having the maximum dose of fludrocortisone, consider sodium chloride supplementation according to specialist endocrinology advice.

mcqs.question: Which routes does NICE say shouldn't be used for routine daily hydrocortisone replacement?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not offer hydrocortisone by subcutaneous pump or IM/IV administration for routine daily replacement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not offer hydrocortisone by subcutaneous pump or intramuscular or intravenous administration for routine daily replacement.

mcqs.question: What does NICE advise about increasing glucocorticoid doses in adrenal insufficiency?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not increase glucocorticoid dosing for a long duration, because of the risk of over-replacement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not increase glucocorticoid dosing for a long duration (see signs and symptoms of glucocorticoid over-replacement in box 1 ).

mcqs.question: An adult on oral prednisolone 10 mg daily or more asks about sick-day dosing. What does NICE advise?

options.A: Stop prednisolone during illness and restart once the person has recovered
options.C: No extra dose needed; may split into 2
options.E: Triple the dose for any cold

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No extra dose needed; may split into 2
mcqs.explanation: NICE: people on 10 mg or more of prednisolone daily don't need additional sick-day dosing but can split the total daily dose into 2 equal doses.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Advise people taking a daily oral prednisolone dose of 10 mg or more that they do not need additional sick-day dosing, but they can split their total daily dose into 2 equal doses.
