mcqs.question: A ward patient has been on IV co-amoxiclav for 60 hours. What does NICE suggest at this point?

options.A: Review: continue, stop, or switch to oral
options.B: Automatically continue IV therapy for a full 7-day course

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Review: continue, stop, or switch to oral
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider reviewing IV antimicrobial prescriptions at 48–72 hours, including response and microbiology, to decide whether to continue and whether to switch to oral.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider reviewing intravenous antimicrobial prescriptions at 48–72 hours in all health and care settings (including community and outpatient services). Include response to treatment and microbiological results in any review, to determine if the antimicrobial needs to be continued and, if so, whether it can be switched to an oral antimicrobial.

mcqs.question: Which principles does NICE say prescribers should follow from local or national guidelines when prescribing antimicrobials?

options.A: IV route for all moderate infections
options.B: The longest course possible, to prevent relapse and resistance
options.D: Shortest effective course, right dose and route

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Shortest effective course, right dose and route
mcqs.explanation: NICE: follow guidelines on prescribing the shortest effective course, the most appropriate dose and route of administration.

sourceRefs.excerpt: When prescribing antimicrobials, prescribers should follow local (where available) or national guidelines on: prescribing the shortest effective course; the most appropriate dose; route of administration.

mcqs.question: A patient likely has a self-limiting viral sore throat. What does NICE advise about immediate antimicrobial prescription?

options.E: Prescribe a broad-spectrum agent to cover secondary bacterial infection

mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not issue an immediate antimicrobial prescription to a patient likely to have a self-limiting condition.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not issue an immediate prescription for an antimicrobial to a patient who is likely to have a self‑limiting condition.

mcqs.question: For a patient with a non-severe infection, when does NICE suggest taking microbiological samples before deciding on antimicrobials?

options.C: Never; always prescribe first and sample only if treatment fails
options.D: When it's safe to wait for results

mcqs.correctAnswerText: When it's safe to wait for results
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider taking samples before deciding to prescribe, provided it's safe to withhold treatment until results are available.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For patients who have non‑severe infections, consider taking microbiological samples before making a decision about prescribing an antimicrobial, providing it is safe to withhold treatment until the results are available.

mcqs.question: A primary care patient has a recurrent infection. What does NICE suggest?

options.A: Prescribe a different antibiotic each time
options.B: Send samples when prescribing; review results
options.D: Refer urgently to infectious diseases before any further prescribing

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Send samples when prescribing; review results
mcqs.explanation: NICE: for recurrent or persistent infections in primary care, consider taking samples when prescribing and review when results are available.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For patients in primary care who have recurrent or persistent infections, consider taking microbiological samples when prescribing an antimicrobial and review the prescription when the results are available.

mcqs.question: Which factors does NICE say to consider for an individual patient once the decision to prescribe an antimicrobial is made?

options.C: Only the prescriber's usual preference for that infection site

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider interactions with medicines and food/drink, other illnesses (e.g. renal dose adjustment), drug allergies and other individual factors.

sourceRefs.excerpt: When a decision to prescribe an antimicrobial has been made, take into account the benefits and harms for an individual patient associated with the particular antimicrobial, including: possible interactions with other medicines or any food and drink; the patient's other illnesses, for example, the need for dose adjustment in a patient with renal impairment; any drug allergies (see the NICE guideline on drug allergy ; these should be documented in the patient's record); the risk of selection for

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend about repeat antimicrobial prescriptions?

options.A: Repeat any course the patient requests
options.C: Only when indicated; review within 6 months
options.D: Issue freely for any recurrent symptom
options.E: Allow repeat courses for up to 2 years without a formal review

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Only when indicated; review within 6 months
mcqs.explanation: NICE: don't issue repeat prescriptions unless needed for a particular indication. Avoid repeats longer than 6 months without review.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not issue repeat prescriptions for antimicrobials unless needed for a particular clinical condition or indication. Avoid issuing repeat prescriptions for longer than 6 months without review and ensure adequate monitoring for individual patients to reduce adverse drug reactions and to check whether continuing an antimicrobial is really needed.

mcqs.question: What safety-netting advice does NICE say everyone with an infection should get, whether or not they're given antimicrobials?

options.A: None if no antimicrobial is given
options.B: Only how to finish the full course of tablets, even if they feel better
options.E: Duration, worsening, side effects, when to return

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Duration, worsening, side effects, when to return
mcqs.explanation: NICE: share safety-netting advice including how long symptoms are likely to last with and without antimicrobials, what to do if worse or if adverse effects occur, and when to seek advice again.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Share safety-netting advice with everyone who has an infection (regardless of whether or not they are prescribed or supplied with antimicrobials). This should include: how long symptoms are likely to last with and without antimicrobials; what to do if symptoms get worse; what to do if they experience adverse effects from the treatment; when they should ask again for medical advice.

mcqs.question: When does NICE accept prescribing antimicrobials after a remote assessment alone?

options.A: Whenever the patient requests it and has had antibiotics before
options.C: Sound reason, and the person knows how to get help

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Sound reason, and the person knows how to get help
mcqs.explanation: NICE: don't routinely prescribe remotely unless the person knows when and how to seek help and there's a sound reason (e.g. can't attend, severity can be assessed, low risk of alternative diagnosis).

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not routinely prescribe antimicrobials based on a remote assessment alone unless the person knows when and how to seek further medical help and there is a sound reason to prescribe remotely, for example: the person cannot or would find it very difficult to attend a face-to-face appointment and/or the severity of illness can be adequately assessed remotely and the risk of an alternative diagnosis is low and the prescriber is confident that antimicrobials are needed.

mcqs.question: Which core members does NICE say an antimicrobial stewardship team should include?

options.B: Only an infection prevention and control nurse with a ward manager

mcqs.explanation: NICE: AMS teams should have core members including an antimicrobial pharmacist and a medical microbiologist, and can co-opt others.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Organisations establishing antimicrobial stewardship teams should ensure that the team has core members (including an antimicrobial pharmacist and a medical microbiologist) and can co-opt additional members depending on the care setting and the antimicrobial issue being considered.

mcqs.question: How does NICE suggest evaluating the effectiveness of stewardship interventions?

options.E: Measure drug acquisition costs only, compared with the previous year

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider evaluating effectiveness by reviewing rates and trends of antimicrobial prescribing and resistance.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider evaluating the effectiveness of antimicrobial stewardship interventions by reviewing rates and trends of antimicrobial prescribing and resistance.

mcqs.question: A prescriber repeatedly prescribes antimicrobials outside local guidelines without justification. What does NICE suggest?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: provide feedback and advice to prescribers who prescribe outside local guidelines when it isn't justified.

sourceRefs.excerpt: provide feedback and advice to prescribers who prescribe antimicrobials outside of local guidelines when it is not justified.

mcqs.question: What culture does NICE encourage around antimicrobial prescribing among colleagues?

options.D: Hierarchical; only consultants may question antimicrobial decisions

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider peer review systems and encourage an open, transparent culture in which health professionals can question colleagues' prescribing when it's not in line with guidelines.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider developing local systems and processes for peer review of prescribing. Encourage an open and transparent culture that allows health professionals to question antimicrobial prescribing practices of colleagues when these are not in line with local (where available) or national guidelines and no reason is documented.

mcqs.question: Which pack-size approach does NICE suggest to support stewardship?

options.C: Packs with extra tablets 'just in case' symptoms recur after the course

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider supplying antimicrobials in pack sizes that correspond to local or national guideline course lengths.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider supplying antimicrobials in pack sizes that correspond to local (where available) and national guidelines on course lengths.

mcqs.question: When a new antimicrobial is introduced locally, which approaches to support it does NICE suggest?

options.A: E-alerts and guidance on when to use it
options.C: Withhold it from the formulary indefinitely

mcqs.correctAnswerText: E-alerts and guidance on when to use it
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider multiple approaches, such as electronic alerts and prescribing guidance on when and where to use the new antimicrobial.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider using multiple approaches to support the introduction of a new antimicrobial, including: electronic alerts to notify prescribers about the antimicrobial; prescribing guidance about when and where to use the antimicrobial in practice; issuing new or updated formulary guidelines and antimicrobial prescribing guidelines; peer advocacy and advice from other prescribers; providing education or informal teaching on ward rounds; shared risk management strategies for antimicrobials that are pot

mcqs.question: According to the Dutch Working Party on Antibiotic Policy (2023), what's an important aspect of antibiotic stewardship?
mcqs.explanation: SWAB 2023: prudent handling of reported antibiotic allergies is an important aspect of stewardship.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Dutch Working Party on Antibiotic Policy (SWAB)
sourceRefs.excerpt: Prudent handling of reported antibiotic allergies is an important aspect of antibiotic stewardship.

mcqs.question: Across which care settings do commissioners need antimicrobial stewardship to operate, according to NICE?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: commissioners should ensure AMS operates across all care settings as part of a stewardship programme.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Commissioners should ensure that antimicrobial stewardship operates across all care settings as part of an antimicrobial stewardship programme.

mcqs.question: What was the clinical concern behind the 2012 trial of antimicrobial prophylaxis for flexible urethrocystoscopy?

options.B: Urethral stricture caused by the flexible scope itself
options.D: UTI risk and lack of consensus on prophylaxis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: UTI risk and lack of consensus on prophylaxis
mcqs.explanation: The main drawback of flexible urethrocystoscopy is UTI risk, and there's no unanimous view on prophylaxis indications, dose or type.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Objectives One of the main drawbacks of flexible urethrocystoscopy is the risk of urinary tract infection (UTI). In order to reduce this risk, antimicrobial prophylaxis has been considered, however there is not a unanimous view regarding indications, dosage, type of antibiotic, and so on. To

topics.topicKey: adrenal crisis hydrocortisone emergency protocol trigger avoidance sick day rules
topics.topicDisplayName: Adrenal crisis: hydrocortisone emergency protocol, trigger avoidance, sick day rules
topics.coverageNote: Pool: NICE NG243 adrenal insufficiency (no stored year; 2024), Japan Endocrine Society 2016/2019, and trials. There's no stored row giving the acute crisis dose of hydrocortisone (100 mg IV/IM bolus, then 200 mg/24 h) or fluid resuscitation; the only stated 100 mg IM dose is for mental health crisis. Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance is missing.

mcqs.question: A patient with known primary adrenal insufficiency is critically unwell with hypotension, hyponatraemia and hypoglycaemia. Which reversible cause does NICE say to consider?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider adrenal crisis in critically unwell people with low BP, hyperpigmentation (primary), hyponatraemia, hypoglycaemia, shock, or failure to respond to initial treatment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider adrenal crisis as a potentially reversible cause in people who are critically unwell with any of the following: low blood pressure (including postural hypotension); hyperpigmentation ( primary adrenal insufficiency only); hyponatraemia; hypoglycaemia (particularly in children); circulatory shock or collapse; condition failing to respond to initial treatments.

mcqs.question: Which milder presentation does NICE say should still prompt consideration of adrenal crisis in someone at high risk?

options.E: Isolated mild headache that settles with simple analgesia

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider crisis in people with, or at high risk of, AI who are unwell with milder symptoms such as lethargy, pallor, clamminess, feeling cold or feverish, confusion and weakness.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider adrenal crisis in people with, or at high risk of, adrenal insufficiency (see recommendation 1.2.1 ) who are unwell with milder symptoms, including: lethargy; pallor; clamminess; feeling cold or feverish; confusion or altered mental states; weakness.

mcqs.question: During significant physiological stress, what minimum oral glucocorticoid dose does NICE recommend for people with adrenal insufficiency?

options.C: Hydrocortisone 200 mg as a single oral dose on the first day only

mcqs.explanation: NICE: at least 40 mg oral hydrocortisone daily in 2–4 divided doses, or at least 10 mg prednisolone daily in 1–2 doses, until the illness or trauma resolves.

sourceRefs.excerpt: During periods of significant physiological stress, offer at least 40 mg oral hydrocortisone daily in 2 to 4 divided doses or at least 10 mg oral prednisolone daily in 1 to 2 divided doses until the acute illness or physical trauma has resolved.

mcqs.question: A patient takes modified-release hydrocortisone. What does NICE say about their supplies for sick days?

options.B: Double the modified-release capsule dose for the duration of illness

mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer additional oral glucocorticoid supplies for sick-day dosing. On MR hydrocortisone, provide immediate-release hydrocortisone.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer additional supplies of oral glucocorticoids to cover increased dosing during periods of physiological stress ( sick-day dosing ). For people on modified-release hydrocortisone, provide supplies of immediate-release hydrocortisone. See recommendation 1.1.4 for information and support on sick-day rules .

mcqs.question: Which patients does NICE suggest considering for an emergency management kit?

options.A: Aged 16+ with tertiary AI and previous crisis
options.E: Anyone after a short course of prednisolone, regardless of history

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Aged 16+ with tertiary AI and previous crisis
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider an emergency kit for people aged 16 and over with tertiary AI and a history of adrenal crisis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider giving people aged 16 and over with tertiary adrenal insufficiency and a history of adrenal crisis an emergency management kit.

mcqs.question: Which injection should an adrenal insufficiency emergency kit contain, according to NICE?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: kits should include IM hydrocortisone (premixed hydrocortisone sodium phosphate 100 mg/1 ml or succinate 100 mg powder), needles, syringes and easy-to-follow instructions.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Each emergency kit should contain: an intramuscular hydrocortisone injection; premixed hydrocortisone sodium phosphate 100 mg/1 ml (1 vial), or hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg powder and 5 ml or 10 ml water for injection (1 vial); two blue needles; two 2 ml syringes; written instructions in an easy-to-understand format (for example, with diagrams or pictures) on how to prepare and give emergency intramuscular hydrocortisone and how to safely dispose of needles and syringes; steroid emerge

mcqs.question: A person with adrenal insufficiency is in severe mental health crisis and can't take oral glucocorticoids. What does NICE suggest?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider sick-day dosing in severe mental health crisis, and 100 mg IM hydrocortisone if oral glucocorticoids can't be taken.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider sick-day dosing (see recommendation 1.4.2 ) at times of severe mental health crisis (for example, a psychotic episode). Consider giving 100 mg of intramuscular hydrocortisone for a person in severe mental health crisis who is unable to take oral glucocorticoids.

mcqs.question: An adult with adrenal insufficiency is facing significant psychological stress. What does NICE suggest?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider sick-day dosing for 1 or 2 days during psychological stress.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider sick-day dosing (see recommendation 1.4.2 ) for 1 or 2 days during psychological stress .

mcqs.question: For children under 16 with adrenal insufficiency experiencing psychological stress, which guidance does NICE refer to?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider 1 or 2 sick-day doses and follow section 5 of the BSPED consensus guidelines.

sourceRefs.excerpt: For babies, children and young people up to 16 years experiencing psychological stress, consider 1 or 2 sick-day doses and follow section 5 in the British Society of Paediatric Endocrinology and Diabetes (BSPED) consensus guidelines on adrenal insufficiency .

mcqs.question: Which patients does NICE say should be offered a blue steroid treatment card?

options.A: Exogenous GC users at risk of tertiary AI
options.E: Only solid-organ transplant recipients on long-term immunosuppression

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Exogenous GC users at risk of tertiary AI
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer blue steroid treatment cards to people on exogenous glucocorticoids for non-endocrine conditions who are at risk of tertiary AI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer blue steroid treatment cards to people on exogenous glucocorticoids for non-endocrine conditions who are at risk of tertiary adrenal insufficiency .

mcqs.question: A patient on prednisolone at physiological equivalent dose is tired. A colleague requests a cortisol test. What does NICE advise?

options.A: Do a short Synacthen test now, without changing the prednisolone
options.D: Don't test while on these doses

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Don't test while on these doses
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not test for adrenal insufficiency in people taking oral glucocorticoids at physiological equivalent doses or above.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not test for adrenal insufficiency in people taking oral glucocorticoids at physiological equivalent doses or above.

mcqs.question: Which first test does NICE recommend for suspected adrenal insufficiency in people aged 1 year and over?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: offer an 8 am to 9 am serum cortisol test and interpret it using table 1.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Offer an 8 am to 9 am serum cortisol test to people aged 1 year and over with suspected adrenal insufficiency. Follow table 1 to interpret the results and aid decision making.

mcqs.question: What does NICE say about cortisol day series for checking hydrocortisone dosing?

options.A: Do them after any dose change
options.D: Use them in place of clinical review

mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not routinely carry out cortisol day series to check hydrocortisone dosing.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not routinely carry out cortisol day series to check hydrocortisone dosing.

mcqs.question: Which diagnostic approach for adrenal insufficiency does the Japan Endocrine Society (2016) recommend?

options.E: Basal cortisol and ACTH plus 250 µg ACTH test

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Basal cortisol and ACTH plus 250 µg ACTH test
mcqs.explanation: JES 2016: measure basal cortisol and ACTH in combination with a rapid ACTH (250 µg corticotropin) test.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Diagnosis of adrenal insufficiency should include measurement of basal cortisol and ACTH levels in combination with a rapid ACTH (250 µg corticotropin) test.

mcqs.question: Why does the Japan Endocrine Society (2019) stress managing endocrine irAEs from immune checkpoint inhibitors?

options.A: They can cause life-threatening adrenal crisis
options.E: They only occur after immune checkpoint inhibitors have been stopped

mcqs.correctAnswerText: They can cause life-threatening adrenal crisis
mcqs.explanation: JES 2019: managing endocrine irAEs from ICIs is crucial because of potential life-threatening consequences such as adrenal crisis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Management of immune-related adverse events in endocrine organs induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors is crucial due to the potential for life-threatening consequences like adrenal crisis.

mcqs.question: In cancer patients receiving antiemetic dexamethasone, which drug was associated with secondary adrenal suppression (2015 study)?
mcqs.explanation: Megestrol acetate was significantly associated with secondary adrenal suppression (OR 3.06, 95% CI 1.60–5.86). About 15% developed suppression.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Multivariate analysis revealed that secondary adrenal suppression associated with antiemetic dexamethasone therapy was significantly associated with megestrol acetate treatment (odds ratio: 3.06; 95% confidence interval: 1.60 to 5.86; p Conclusion This large prospective study indicates that approximately 15% of cancer patients receiving chemotherapy with a normal adrenal response s

mcqs.question: What does NICE advise for people tapering glucocorticoids below physiological equivalent doses?

options.A: Daily serum cortisol levels throughout the taper
options.C: Monitor for AI; advise family and carers

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Monitor for AI; advise family and carers
mcqs.explanation: NICE: monitor for signs and symptoms of AI during tapering below physiological doses, and advise family and carers.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Monitor people on glucocorticoid dose tapering below physiological equivalent dose regimens for signs and symptoms of adrenal insufficiency (see the section on when to suspect adrenal insufficiency ) and provide advice to family and carers about potential symptoms to expect.

mcqs.question: In the 2015 COPD exacerbation study of HPA axis changes, what was the outcome related to adrenal crisis?

options.A: Adrenal crisis occurred in about half of patients during follow-up
options.E: No hospitalisations or deaths from crisis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No hospitalisations or deaths from crisis
mcqs.explanation: There were no hospitalisations or deaths from adrenal crisis, although dynamic HPA axis changes occurred.

sourceRefs.excerpt: There were no hospitalizations or deaths as a result of adrenal crisis. Conclusion Dynamic changes in the HPA axis occur during and after the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD.

mcqs.question: Which persistent features does NICE list as prompts to consider adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: Tremor, heat intolerance and weight loss with a raised free T4

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider AI with unexplained hyperpigmentation or persistent weight loss, salt craving, GI symptoms, postural dizziness, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia or lethargy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider adrenal insufficiency in people with unexplained hyperpigmentation, or when there is no other clinical explanation for the presence of 1 or more of the following persistent symptoms, signs or features: weight loss; salt craving; nausea or vomiting; lack of appetite or unable to eat a full meal; diarrhoea; dizziness or light-headedness on standing; hyponatraemia; hyperkalaemia; lethargy; early puberty; feeling of muscle weakness; hypoglycaemia (particularly in children); faltering growth

mcqs.question: A person with adrenal insufficiency previously declined education about sick-day rules. What does NICE advise?

options.A: Don't raise it again, to respect their earlier decision

mcqs.explanation: NICE: continue to offer information and support even if it has been declined previously.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Continue to offer information and support to people with adrenal insufficiency even if this has been declined previously.

mcqs.question: Which drug does the VA/DoD (2024) recommend for prevention of chronic tension-type headache?

sourceRefs.sourceBody: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and U.S. Department of Defense
sourceRefs.excerpt: Amitriptyline should be used for prevention of chronic tension-type headache.

mcqs.question: What does the VA/DoD (2023) suggest primary care clinicians consider for treatment and prevention of TTH?
mcqs.explanation: VA/DoD 2023: consider tricyclic antidepressants and lifestyle interventions for TTH treatment and prevention.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Primary care clinicians should consider tricyclic antidepressants and lifestyle interventions for the treatment and prevention of tension-type headache.

mcqs.question: Which acute treatments does NICE suggest considering for tension-type headache?

options.D: Oral triptans, taken at the first sign of headache

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider aspirin, paracetamol or an NSAID, taking into account preference, comorbidities and adverse event risk.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider aspirin, paracetamol or an NSAID for the acute treatment of tension‑type headache, taking into account the person's preference, comorbidities and risk of adverse events. Because of the association with Reye's syndrome, preparations containing aspirin should not be offered to under 16s. [2012]

mcqs.question: A 14-year-old has episodic tension-type headache. Which acute analgesic does NICE say shouldn't be offered?

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider aspirin, paracetamol or an NSAID for the acute treatment of tension‑type headache, taking into account the person's preference, comorbidities and risk of adverse events. Because of the association with Reye's syndrome, preparations containing aspirin should not be offered to under 16s. [2012]

mcqs.question: A patient with frequent TTH asks for codeine. What's the NICE position on opioids for acute TTH?

options.B: Use them for up to 10 days a month

mcqs.question: Which non-drug prophylaxis does NICE suggest considering for chronic TTH?

options.A: Weekly spinal manipulation sessions continued for 1 year

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider a course of up to 10 sessions of acupuncture over 5 to 8 weeks for the prophylactic treatment of chronic tension-type headache . [2012]

mcqs.question: What's the AAN (2016) position on onabotulinumtoxinA for chronic tension-type headache?

options.E: First-line prophylaxis for chronic TTH in primary care

mcqs.explanation: AAN 2016: onabotulinumtoxinA is probably ineffective for chronic TTH and should not be offered.

sourceRefs.excerpt: OnabotulinumtoxinA is probably ineffective for chronic tension-type headaches and should not be offered.

mcqs.question: What does the Chiropractic Association (2011) guideline conclude about spinal manipulation for episodic TTH?

options.E: It works only for chronic TTH

mcqs.explanation: Spinal manipulation cannot be recommended for the management of episodic TTH.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Spinal manipulation cannot be recommended for the management of episodic tension-type headache.

mcqs.question: Which therapies does the EHF/Lifting the Burden (2019) describe as useful for TTH when drugs must be avoided?
mcqs.explanation: EHF 2019: biofeedback and relaxation therapies can help and are potentially useful when drug treatments must be avoided.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: European Headache Federation and Lifting The Burden
sourceRefs.excerpt: Biofeedback and relaxation therapies can be helpful and are potentially useful options when drug treatments must be avoided for tension-type headache management.

mcqs.question: What does the EHF (2019) say about herbal treatments for headache?

options.A: Preferable to simple analgesics for frequent episodic headache
options.D: Not recommended: limited evidence, interaction risk

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Not recommended: limited evidence, interaction risk
mcqs.explanation: EHF 2019: herbals are not recommended. Trial data are limited, there's no evidence of safety in prolonged use, and they may interact with other medicines.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: European Headache Federation and Lifting The Burden
sourceRefs.excerpt: Herbals are not recommended for headache treatment. Clinical trials data are limited and provide no evidence of safety in prolonged use, and herbals may interfere with other medications.

mcqs.question: Which magnesium regimen does the EHF (2019) suggest may be tried for headache?

options.B: Citrate 1 g tds from the start
options.C: Citrate 100 mg tds, up to 200 mg tds

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Citrate 100 mg tds, up to 200 mg tds
mcqs.explanation: EHF 2019: magnesium citrate starting at 100 mg three times daily (to avoid diarrhoea), increasing to 200 mg three times daily.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: European Headache Federation and Lifting The Burden
sourceRefs.excerpt: Magnesium (as citrate, starting at 100 mg three times daily to avoid diarrhoea, and increasing to 200 mg three times daily) may be tried for headache management where preparations of pharmaceutical quality are available.

mcqs.question: A patient with recurrent TTH fears a brain tumour. What does the EHF (2019) emphasise?

options.D: Education and reassurance should never be omitted
options.E: Arrange an MRI scan to reassure them that there's no tumour

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Education and reassurance should never be omitted
mcqs.explanation: EHF 2019: education and appropriate reassurance should never be omitted in recurrent headache with unfounded fear of underlying disease.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: European Headache Federation and Lifting The Burden
sourceRefs.excerpt: Education and appropriate reassurance should never be omitted in patients with recurrent headache who wrongly fear underlying disease.

mcqs.question: A patient with typical TTH and no red flags requests a brain scan for reassurance. What does NICE advise?

options.B: Arrange MRI head to exclude a structural cause and reassure
options.C: Don't refer for imaging solely for reassurance

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Don't refer for imaging solely for reassurance
mcqs.explanation: NICE: do not refer people with TTH, migraine, cluster headache or MOH for neuroimaging solely for reassurance.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not refer people diagnosed with tension‑type headache, migraine, cluster headache or medication overuse headache for neuroimaging solely for reassurance. [2012]

mcqs.question: What does NICE suggest a headache diary can be used for?

options.D: Deciding on neuroimaging alone, without a clinical assessment

mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider a headache diary to record frequency, duration and severity, monitor intervention effectiveness, and support discussion.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider using a headache diary: to record the frequency, duration and severity of headaches; to monitor the effectiveness of headache interventions; as a basis for discussion with the person about their headache disorder and its impact. [2012]

mcqs.question: How often must headaches occur before the German Migraine and Headache Society (2011) recommends physician visits?
mcqs.explanation: The German society recommends physician visits for headaches on more than 10 days per month.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Deutsche Migräne und Kopfschmerzgesellschaft, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Neurologie, Österreichische Kopfschmerzgesellschaft, Schweizerische Kopfwehgesellschaft
sourceRefs.excerpt: Physician visits are recommended for patients with headaches occurring more than 10 days per month.

mcqs.question: A patient with TTH presents with a new sudden-onset headache reaching maximum intensity within 5 minutes. What does NICE advise?

options.C: Reassure, give analgesia and review in 3 months if it persists

mcqs.explanation: NICE: sudden-onset headache reaching maximum intensity within 5 minutes is a feature that warrants evaluation and consideration of investigation or referral.

Consider further investigations and/or referral if a person diagnosed with a headache disorder develops any of the features listed in recommendation 1.1.1. [2012]

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend for medication overuse headache, alongside withdrawal of the overused medicine?

options.B: Inpatient withdrawal for everyone, followed by an opioid taper
options.D: Consider prophylaxis for the primary headache

mcqs.question: What does NICE recommend about the setting for withdrawal in medication overuse headache?

options.C: Always as an inpatient, under specialist supervision

mcqs.question: According to the EAN (2020), who should manage medication-overuse headache?

mcqs.question: In the 2015 trial of a brief intervention for medication-overuse headache, what was the reduction in headache days per month compared with usual care?

mcqs.question: Which patients does NICE say need lifelong intramuscular vitamin B12?

mcqs.question: Oral B12 is being used for deficiency caused or suspected to be caused by malabsorption. What minimum dose does NICE recommend?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: prescribe at least 1 mg a day for oral replacement in malabsorption.

sourceRefs.excerpt: When offering oral vitamin B12 replacement to people with vitamin B12 deficiency caused, or suspected to be caused, by malabsorption, prescribe a dosage of at least 1 mg a day.

mcqs.question: Which oral B12 dose does NICE suggest considering in pregnancy or breastfeeding?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider at least 1 mg a day when offering oral B12 in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

sourceRefs.excerpt: When offering oral vitamin B12 replacement in pregnancy or during breastfeeding, consider a dosage of at least 1 mg a day.

mcqs.question: When does NICE recommend the first follow-up appointment after starting B12 replacement?

options.E: 6 months for everyone, including pregnant women

mcqs.question: What does NICE advise about repeating the initial diagnostic test during IM B12 replacement?

mcqs.question: When does NICE suggest an anti-intrinsic factor antibody test?

options.B: Suspected autoimmune gastritis, not tested before

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Suspected autoimmune gastritis, not tested before
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider anti-IF antibodies if autoimmune gastritis is suspected and there has been no previous positive test or absorption-affecting surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider an anti-intrinsic factor antibody test for people with vitamin B12 deficiency if autoimmune gastritis is suspected and they have not previously had: a positive anti-intrinsic factor antibody test at any time or an operation that could affect vitamin B12 absorption (such as total gastrectomy or complete terminal ileal resection).

mcqs.question: B12 deficiency is suspected as a side effect of a medicine. What does NICE suggest while awaiting results?
mcqs.explanation: NICE: consider starting B12 replacement while waiting for results in suspected medicine-induced deficiency.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider starting vitamin B12 replacement while waiting for the test results of people with suspected vitamin B12 deficiency that is a side effect of taking medicine (see recommendation 1.5.7 in the section on managing medicine-induced deficiency ).

mcqs.question: Which replacement does NICE recommend for B12 deficiency caused by recreational nitrous oxide use?
